evidence.quote: Let $D$ be a connected polydisc, and let $p:\mathcal X\to D$ be a smooth proper holomorphic family of $n$-dimensional varieties, $n\geq2$, with a relative embedding in $D\times\mathbb P^N$. Let $$\theta\in H^0(D,R^4p_*\mathbb Q)$$ be a flat rational class. outputs.exact_statement: Suppose $\operatorname{Hg}(V)=\operatorname{SO}(V,q)$. The following conditions are equivalent.* 1. *There are an abelian variety $B$ and a cycle $\alpha\in\operatorname{CH}^2(S\times B)_{\mathbb Q}$ such that $$\alpha_*:V\longrightarrow H^2(B,\mathbb Q)$$ is nonzero.* 2. *There are a smooth connected projective surface $Y$ and a dominant generically finite morphism $f:Y\to S$ such that $$\label{eq:wedge-condition} f_*\!\left(\operatorname{im}\!\left[ \bigwedge\nolimits^2 H^0(Y,\Omega_Y^1) \longrightarrow H^0(Y,\Omega_Y^2)\right]\right)\ne0.$$* 3. *The prescribed full Kuga–Satake map is realized as in [eq:cycle-target], for any stipulated standard data on $T$.* *In this situation $T=V$. The same input realizes the standard map for the full primitive Clifford construction with the cup form.

Fix a component of the moduli space of primitively amply polarized K3 surfaces of degree $2d$. Assume that condition (i) or condition (ii) of Theorem 1 holds very generally in that component. Then every $(S,h)$ in the component satisfies [eq:cycle-target], with all the stipulated standard data on $T(S)$.* *Here it suffices that, about each desired point, the input holds outside a countable union of proper closed analytic subsets of a full polarized period chart. In particular an input outside countably many proper algebraic subsets of the moduli component suffices. The witness cycles, abelian varieties, or surface covers need not vary in a family.
If the hypothesis of Theorem 2 holds in the required polarized components in every degree, then [eq:cycle-target] holds for every projective K3 surface.

For complex abelian varieties $P,Q$, pullback identifies $$\operatorname{Hom}(Q,P)\otimes\mathbb Q
 \simeq
 \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{HS}}\bigl(H^1(P,\mathbb Q),H^1(Q,\mathbb Q)\bigr).$$ Thus arbitrary rational weight-one Hodge maps can act algebraically and independently on the two factors of an ordered tensor product of first cohomology groups.

Every cohomological Künneth projector on a product of abelian varieties is induced by a rational algebraic correspondence. If $U=H^1(B,\mathbb Q)$ and $m:B\times B\to B$ is addition, then the mixed part of $m^*$ gives an injection $$H^2(B,\mathbb Q)=\bigwedge\nolimits^2U\longrightarrow U\otimes U,
 \qquad u\wedge v\longmapsto u\otimes v-v\otimes u.$$

Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional rational vector space of cohomological maps, and let $E_{\mathrm{alg}}\subset E$ be the image of rational algebraic correspondences of a fixed degree. For every field extension $K/\mathbb Q$, $$E\cap(E_{\mathrm{alg}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}K)=E_{\mathrm{alg}}
 \quad\text{inside }E\otimes_{\mathbb Q}K.$$ The same assertion holds if only a specified rational subspace of the source is considered.
Conditions (i) and (ii) of Theorem 1 are equivalent. The implication from the surface condition to a nonzero correspondence on $V$ does not require the full Hodge-group hypothesis.

Suppose $f:H(1)\to\operatorname{Hom}(P,M)$ is algebraically realized. For rational weight-one Hodge maps $a:M\to M'$ and $b:P'\to P$, the map $x\mapsto a f(x)b$ is algebraically realized. The same holds after changing the chosen duality isomorphisms, interchanging the tensor factors, or making rational weight-one Hodge identifications with isogenous abelian models.

In any sufficiently small, full-dimensional marked polarized period chart, Equation [gen:full-group] holds outside a countable union of proper closed analytic subsets. At every point satisfying Equation [gen:full-group], the Hodge structure $V$ is irreducible and $T(S)=V$.

There is a decomposition into commuting rational ideals $$\mathfrak h=\mathfrak g\oplus\mathfrak k,
 \qquad \mathfrak g\simeq\mathfrak{so}(V,q),$$ where $\mathfrak k$ is the kernel of the action on $V$. The ideal $\mathfrak k$ acts trivially on $W^+$ and $W^-$, and $\mathfrak g$ acts on them by the usual left spin action.

The space $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g_{\mathbb C}}
 (V_{\mathbb C},\Delta\otimes\Delta)$ has dimension one. Neither $\Delta$ nor the trivial representation contains a vector copy $V_{\mathbb C}$.

Assume Equation [gen:full-group]. Suppose that $\alpha\in\operatorname{CH}^2(S\times B)_{\mathbb Q}$ induces a nonzero map $V\to H^2(B,\mathbb Q)$ for some complex abelian variety $B$. Let $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\in\{+,-\}$, and let $A_1,A_2$ be abelian varieties realizing $W^{\epsilon_1},W^{\epsilon_2}$ as their first rational cohomology. Every rational Hodge map $$\beta:V\longrightarrow W^{\epsilon_1}\otimes W^{\epsilon_2} \subset H^2(A_1\times A_2,\mathbb Q)$$ is the restriction of the action of a cycle $\Gamma\in\operatorname{CH}^2(S\times A_1\times A_2)_{\mathbb Q}$. In particular, this recovers the full primitive Clifford multiplication tensor and its prescribed even-Clifford realization.

Let $p:\mathcal X\to D$ be a smooth proper holomorphic family of nonempty, pure $n$-dimensional varieties over a connected complex manifold. Suppose that an embedding $$\mathcal X\hookrightarrow D\times\mathbb P^N$$ over $D$ has been given. There are a reduced complex quasi-projective scheme $H$, a smooth projective algebraic family $\mathcal U\to H$, and a holomorphic map $\eta:D\to H^{\mathrm{an}}$ such that $\mathcal X$ is the embedded analytic pullback of $\mathcal U$.

Let $f:M\to R$ be a smooth projective algebraic family of relative dimension $n$, with $R$ a smooth irreducible complex variety of dimension $b$. Let $Z\subset M$ be a closed subscheme, flat over $R$, whose fibers have dimension $n-2$. Then $$r\longmapsto
 \operatorname{cl}([Z_r]_{n-2})\in H^4(M_r,\mathbb Q)$$ is a section of the local system $R^4f^{\mathrm{an}}_*\mathbb Q$. This includes nonpure and nonreduced fibers.

Let $D$ be a connected polydisc, and let $p:\mathcal X\to D$ be a smooth proper holomorphic family of $n$-dimensional varieties, $n\geq2$, with a relative embedding in $D\times\mathbb P^N$. Let $$\theta\in H^0(D,R^4p_*\mathbb Q)$$ be a flat rational class. If $\theta_t$ is the class of a rational codimension-two algebraic cycle for very general $t\in D$, then the same holds for every $t\in D$.

Fix a primitively amply polarized K3 surface $(S_0,h)$. After choosing a sufficiently small full-dimensional polarized period polydisc $D$ about its period, there are smooth proper holomorphic families $$\mathcal S\longrightarrow D,
 \qquad \mathcal A\longrightarrow D,$$ with the following properties. The K3 family has central fiber $(S_0,h)$, a relative ample line bundle, and a marking of its integral second cohomology. The primitive rational local system is a fixed quadratic space $(V,q)$ of dimension $21$. The abelian family has marked rational first cohomology $W=C^+(V,q)$ with the full Clifford Hodge structures. Fixed rational polarization and parity-identification data give a flat family of standard tensor maps $$\mu_t:V\longrightarrow H^1(\mathcal A_t,\mathbb Q)
                       \otimes H^1(\mathcal A_t,\mathbb Q).$$ Finally, after shrinking $D$, the product $$\mathcal X=\mathcal S\times_D\mathcal A\times_D\mathcal A$$ admits a relative embedding in $D\times\mathbb P^N$.

Fix a polarized moduli component, and assume that at very general points the nonzero algebraic input of Theorem 1 holds. Then at every $(S_0,h)$ in that component the standard full primitive Clifford tensor is induced by a rational codimension-two algebraic cycle. The same conclusion holds if the hypothesis is made outside countably many proper closed analytic subsets in a full-dimensional polarized period chart about each desired point.
Set $q_0=q|_T$. Algebraic realization of $m^q$ on $V$ implies algebraic realization of $m^{q_0}$ on $T$.

Let $q_0$ and $q_1$ be rational quadratic Hodge polarizations on the same K3-type Hodge structure $T$, allowing either overall sign as in Section 3. If $T\subset H^2(S,\mathbb Q)$ and $m^{q_0}$ is algebraically realized, then so is $m^{q_1}$.
